title: A Two-Stage Data Selection Framework for Data-Efficient Model Training on Edge Devices

problem.claim: Machine learning model training on edge devices faces escalating demand driven by data privacy and personalized service needs.

gap.claim: Current on-device model training under-utilizes on-device data because of low training throughput, limited storage, and diverse data importance.

contributions.claim: Titan is a two-stage data selection framework that selects important data batches from streaming data for model training.
The fine-grained selection stage uses a theoretically optimal strategy to identify the data batch with the highest model performance improvement for the current training round.
Titan pipelines data selection with model training and uses idle computing resources to avoid resource conflicts.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Titan was evaluated on real-world edge devices and three representative edge computing tasks spanning diverse models and data modalities.
The authors report up to 43% lower training time and a 6.2% increase in final accuracy.
The authors report minor system overhead in data processing delay, memory footprint, and energy consumption.

narrative_sequence.summary: Demand for edge-device model training is increasing because of privacy and personalization needs.
Existing on-device training under-utilizes data under throughput, storage, and data-importance constraints.
Titan selects important streaming-data batches through coarse candidate filtering and fine-grained theoretically optimal selection.
A pipeline co-executes data selection and training while using idle computing resources to avoid conflicts.
Evaluation on real-world edge devices and representative tasks is reported to reduce training time and increase final accuracy with minor overhead.

source_observation.claim: The framework first narrows streaming data to a potentially important candidate set before performing fine-grained selection.

interpretation.claim: Separating inexpensive coarse filtering from expensive precise selection can reduce selection cost while retaining focus on high-value data.

application.claim: Resource-constrained training systems may benefit from staged data prioritization aligned with the cost of selection.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify when coarse filtering may discard data needed for the best training outcome.

source_observation.claim: Titan co-executes data selection and model training by exploiting idle computing resources.

interpretation.claim: Overlapping preparation and computation can improve throughput when resource contention is controlled.

application.claim: Edge training pipelines can schedule data preparation alongside training to improve time-and-resource efficiency.

exception.claim: The abstract does not quantify the workload or hardware conditions under which pipeline overlap is beneficial.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the selection objective, optimization formulation, or proof details for the theoretically optimal strategy.
The abstract does not identify the evaluated edge-device configurations, tasks, models, data modalities, baselines, or statistical variation.
The abstract does not define the conditions behind the reported maximum improvements or quantify the stated minor overheads.
